S001@7611-7692.words: do programmes meant to improve education for children and young people with disabilities work
S001@7611-7692.reason: The judgement that nearly all studies were rated low confidence bears on how far the evidence shows whether such programmes work, so a reader needs it to weigh the answer.

S001@7900-8058.reason: The judgement describes the education gap and its cause (school systems not adapted to impairments), not whether any programme improves education or which kinds work best, so it falls under the out-of-scope 'size of the education gap, except as background'.

S001@8059-8153.reason: The judgement concerns interventions to equalise health outcomes, which the scope explicitly excludes when no educational outcome is reported, so it does not bear on whether education programmes for children with disabilities work.

S001@8154-8406.reason: The judgement recommends a twin-track approach (disability-specific support plus inclusion in mainstream activities such as teacher skills and classroom accessibility), which bears directly on which kinds of education programme for children with disabilities work best.

S001@8407-8703.reason: The judgement says most interventions in the review targeted individual children rather than system- or school-level inclusion, which shapes how a reader weighs the evidence on which kinds of programme work best.

S001@8704-8859.reason: The judgement says evaluation should focus on interventions that target the individual's broader environment as well as the individual, which bears on which kinds of programme are assessed and which work best.
